content: Acyclovir cream is specifically used to treat cold sores, also known as fever blisters, which are caused by the herpes simplex virus. These sores typically appear on the face or lips. Acyclovir ointment, on the other hand, is used to manage the first outbreaks of genital herpes, a viral infection caused by the herpes simplex virus that results in sores around the genital and rectal areas. It is also used to treat certain herpes simplex virus-related sores in individuals with weakened immune systems. Acyclovir belongs to a class of antiviral drugs known as synthetic nucleoside analogues. It works by inhibiting the spread of the herpes virus within the body. However, it is important to note that acyclovir does not cure cold sores or genital herpes, nor does it prevent future outbreaks or stop the transmission of these conditions to others. Topical acyclovir is available in two forms: cream and ointment, both of which are applied directly to the skin. Acyclovir cream is typically applied five times a day for four days. It can be used at any stage of a cold sore outbreak but is most effective when applied at the earliest signs of an outbreak, such as tingling, redness, itching, or the appearance of a bump before the sore fully develops. Acyclovir ointment is generally applied six times a day, approximately every three hours, for seven days. It is best to start using the ointment as soon as the first symptoms of infection appear. Always follow the instructions provided on your prescription label and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed, without applying more or less than prescribed. If your symptoms do not improve or worsen during treatment, contact your doctor. Acyclovir cream and ointment are intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, mouth, or nose, and do not ingest the medication. The cream should only be applied to areas of skin where a cold sore has formed or is likely to form. Do not use the cream on unaffected skin or on genital herpes sores. Additionally, do not apply other skin products, such as cosmetics, sunscreen, or lip balm, to the affected area unless instructed by your doctor. When using acyclovir cream, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly. 2. Clean and dry the affected area of skin. 3. Apply a thin layer of cream to cover the area where the cold sore has formed or is likely to form. 4. Gently rub the cream into the skin until it is no longer visible. 5. Leave the treated area uncovered unless your doctor advises otherwise. 6. Wash your hands again with soap and water to remove any residual cream. 7. Avoid washing off the cream from the treated area and refrain from bathing, showering, or swimming immediately after application. 8. Take care not to irritate the cold sore area while using the cream. When using acyclovir ointment, follow these steps: 1. Wear a clean finger cot or rubber glove to apply the ointment. 2. Apply enough ointment to cover all sores completely. 3. Dispose of the used finger cot or glove in a trash can that is out of reach of children. 4. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and avoid wearing tight clothing over the area. If you have any questions, ask your pharmacist or doctor for a copy of the manufacturer's patient information and review it before starting treatment and each time you refill your prescription. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using topical acyclovir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acyclovir, valacyclovir (Valtrex), or any other medications, as well as any ingredients in the cream or ointment. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take, as your doctor may need to adjust dosages or monitor for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have had any conditions affecting your immune system, such as HIV or AIDS. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using acyclovir, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream or ointment to compensate for a missed dose. Topical acyclovir may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dry or cracked lips, flaky or peeling skin, burning or stinging sensations, and redness, swelling, or irritation at the application site. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, and hoarseness, require immediate medical attention. If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container with the cap tightly closed, out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid leaving the medication in your car during extreme temperatures. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of accidental ingestion, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while using this medication. Do not share it with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Brand names for this medication include Zovirax® Cream and Zovirax® Ointment. It is also known by other names, such as Acycloguanosine and ACV.
